requirement.statement: The system SHALL define serializable DomainRef, Presentation, ProjectionPlan, diagnostic, Interaction, Domain Command and Presenter adapter contracts without Vue, DOM, Tiptap, Element Plus, writer or persistence implementations.

case.given: A Projection Presentation selects a presenter for a domain node.
case.then: It SHALL contain only stable presenter ids and serializable data, and SHALL reject executable or ownership-bearing values.

case.given: A non-form XNL dialect compiles a domain tree.
case.then: The generic plan SHALL use open classification ids and SHALL NOT require SchemaEditor group, field, collection, map or union kinds.

requirement.statement: The system SHALL recursively compile generic domain nodes through a code-owned Dialect whose child traversal, classification and transformer processors obey output = fn(runtime, input, config), while Presentation and config remain implementation-free.

case.given: A domain tree contains nested element, array, record and literal nodes.
case.when: The projection compiler compiles the root.
case.then: Every child SHALL be compiled through the runtime recursion capability with deterministic path, role, domain identity, diagnostics and provenance.

case.given: Two independent runtimes compose different ordered Dialect layers.
case.when: The same domain node is compiled in both runtimes.
case.then: Each runtime SHALL resolve only its own later-wins classifier/transformer bindings and SHALL NOT mutate or leak into the other runtime.

case.given: A classification has no bound transformer.
case.then: The compiler SHALL return an explicit unsupported diagnostic and SHALL NOT silently lower to raw JSON or text.

requirement.statement: The support layer SHALL adapt public xnl-core nodes into the generic projection compiler while preserving deterministic tree order and treating explicit #id as domain identity rather than an ordinary editable payload field.

case.given: An XNL tree contains explicit #id values, element body nodes, extend children, arrays and records.
case.when: The default XNL Dialect compiles it.
case.then: The plan SHALL preserve explicit identity, body/extend/array order and deterministic record order without exposing #id as a normal field update.

case.given: The contract, logic and support dependency graph.
case.then: Only support SHALL depend on xnl-core, and no foundation layer SHALL depend on UI or persistence owners.

requirement.statement: The system SHALL render ProjectionPlan as validated surface data through stable Presenter adapter registries and SHALL express Presenter edit intent only as serializable Interaction or Domain Command proposal data without translator, authoring-session or submit authority; Presenter runtime facets SHALL be exact frozen facades constructed from support-owned positive grants under a trusted code-owned protocol, the runtime SHALL exclude arbitrary ungranted source capabilities while allowing a valid source projection to succeed, and SHALL fail closed when facet or grant ownership/shape is invalid or a granted method returns a raw host or unowned object graph, while the protocol remains the review boundary for the authority and internal effects of explicitly granted methods.

case.given: A valid Interaction targets a node in a ProjectionPlan.
case.then: The result SHALL be translated, rejected or unsupported, and SHALL NOT contain an accepted snapshot, mutation writer, ValueHost or VFS capability.

case.given: One valid ProjectionPlan and two renderer-neutral Presenter adapter registries.
case.when: The plan is presented through each registry.
case.then: Both SHALL resolve stable ids and produce distinct surface data from the same plan without modifying the plan or Domain XNL.

case.given: A plan references an unbound presenter id.
case.when: The presentation runner resolves the adapter.
case.then: It SHALL produce an actionable diagnostic and SHALL NOT silently choose a fallback implementation.

case.given: A valid Scope runtime obtained through the existing bindScope or deriveScope path contains granted Presenter-safe capabilities and arbitrary additional ungranted capabilities.
case.when: Trusted code selects a support-owned protocol and constructs a Presenter runtime facet.
case.then: Construction SHALL succeed and expose a new exact frozen facade containing only positive grants; it SHALL exclude the Scope runtime identity, prototype, every ungranted source capability and raw nested host graph, and SHALL resolve the owned facade before invoking the Presenter.

case.given: A caller passes a raw host directly as the view or supplies a forged protocol or facet, an unknown or forged grant, identity projection, a grant targeting an accessor, a facet with an extra own key or a mismatched owner record.
case.when: The factory or presentation runner validates the runtime boundary.
case.then: The system SHALL fail before invoking the Presenter or an accessor and SHALL NOT select a fallback; arbitrary extra ungranted fields on an otherwise valid source SHALL NOT trigger this failure and SHALL instead be excluded because validation SHALL NOT depend on a forbidden-field-name list.

case.given: A trusted code-owned protocol explicitly grants a bound method whose implementation may have internal effects and whose result may be serializable data, an owned facade, a raw host object or another object graph.
case.when: The Presenter invokes the method through its facade wrapper.
case.then: The wrapper SHALL directly return only an immutable serializable snapshot or a facade owned by the same protocol and SHALL throw a closed diagnostic for raw host, foreign authority or unowned object graphs without returning a result envelope; the public grant and protocol types SHALL reject incompatible host/view method arguments or contained return shapes, including narrowing an unknown host result into a concrete facade result; the system SHALL treat the grant as the authority and effect review boundary and SHALL NOT claim to infer closure purity or prevent the method's internal effects.

case.given: A source Scope runtime produced by existing bindScope or deriveScope behavior implements an explicitly granted capability through an object, class, prototype chain or mixin and also has arbitrary additional ungranted capabilities.
case.when: The support protocol forms an independent typed Presenter facet from that source.
case.then: The projected interface SHALL preserve explicitly granted owner-bound method and strong typing semantics while excluding ungranted host possession, and SHALL NOT require any, an open string index signature or raw host casts.

case.given: A renderer-neutral Presenter adapter renders a ProjectionPlan and may express an edit intent.
case.when: The adapter produces normal render output or emits through its edit-intent channel.
case.then: Normal render output SHALL remain validated surface data; edit intent SHALL be serializable Interaction or Domain Command proposal data only, and SHALL contain no translator, authoring session, submit callback or submit authority.
